question: Where does the GPU time of one generated frame go, and which part does FreeFG run with its own shaders?

conditions.test: the project's XeFG SDK test program, headless, output 2560x1440 SDR, engine motion vectors, 2x, GPU timestamps around every dispatch of the frame-generation graph
conditions.freefg: the released proxy (3bb43859), 3 runs x 220 generated frames of the synthetic scene with 1280x720 inputs, 2026-10-18
conditions.intel: Intel's runtime with its own shaders, 1 run x 180 generated frames of replayed game inputs at 2560x1440, 2026-09-27

cross_check.note: Cyberpunk 2077, headless, 2x SDR (figure cyberpunk-2x-fps, same-day block of 2026-10-20 with FreeFG 1.0.0, whose 2x shaders are 0.9.0's): measured FPS change with the proxy against Intel's shaders

notes: Stage times are sums of dispatch times; the gaps between dispatches are not included.

The two bars come from different runs: the Intel reference replayed captured game inputs at 2560x1440, the FreeFG runs used a synthetic scene with 1280x720 inputs (both with 2560x1440 output). Passes that FreeFG leaves to Intel's shaders therefore differ between the bars (the motion splat most: a 320x180 grid against 160x90). The reference run used another variant of Intel's 2x warp, on the same 160x45 grid.

saved_ms includes the difference in the passes that run Intel's shaders in both bars (kept_stages_difference_ms), which comes from the different inputs; saved_in_replaced_stages_ms compares only the stages FreeFG runs with its own shaders.
Intel shaders that FreeFG's own helper passes stand in for (the 224- and 64-channel optical-flow layers) are matched by dispatch grid and call count.
sources: Maintainer evidence, per-dispatch GPU budget of the release pipeline (a later GPU-budget study, 2026-10-19): summary.json rows "sdr-engine-2x" (SDK runs abl1-t-base-sdr-engine-2x-{1,8,15}) and "intel-stock-2x-reference" (SDK replay run replay-long1-stock-2x), from the probe's TIME lines
